title: Insider Trading Policy and Guidelines (including Additional Trading Restrictions for Restricted Persons)

tiers.name: Directors, officers and employees
tiers.description: All Directors, officers and employees of Auckland International Airport Limited and its subsidiaries who intend to trade in Auckland Airport's listed securities. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the confidentiality duty, the one-month short term trading rule and the associated products rule, but not by blackout periods or the consent regime.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors; the Chief Executive, all members of the Senior Leadership Team and their direct reports; the administrative staff of the Executive Offices; trusts and companies controlled by such persons; and anyone else notified by the General Manager Corporate Affairs. Subject to blackout periods, written consent before any trade, and post-trade notification.

tiers.name: all Directors
tiers.description: Distinguished only for consent mechanics: a Director's Request for Consent form must be signed by the Chair or, in the Chair's absence, the Deputy Chair; the Chair's form must be signed by any other Director. Directors also carry the New Zealand relevant-interest disclosure obligations.

tiers.name: the Chief Executive, all members of the Senior Leadership Team and their direct reports
tiers.description: Senior executive population within Restricted Persons. The Chief Executive and the Chief Financial Officer also sign consents on behalf of the Company and approve exceptional-circumstances short term trading.

tiers.name: trusts and companies controlled by such persons
tiers.description: Trusts and companies controlled by a Restricted Person are themselves Restricted Persons; employees and directors are responsible for their actions. Control is not construed technically but by looking at how decisions are made in practice. Spouses and dependants are not separately named.

definitions.hedging_definition: any associated product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any unvested entitlement you are eligible for under that remuneration scheme

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on 30 June of each year
windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement to the NZX of the preliminary final statement or full year results

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on 31 December each year
windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement to the NZX of the half-yearly results

windows.start_anchor: any other period that Auckland Airport specifies from time to time

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Auckland Airport may specify any other blackout period from time to time; the General Manager Corporate Affairs may also notify additional persons that they are Restricted Persons. The Board may approve updates, amendments and exemptions to the Policy, implemented by written notice or posting on the intranet. The Policy does not say whether ad hoc blackouts are confidential.

rules.section: Introduction and purpose; Trading outside black-out periods
rules.detail: Restricted Securities expressly include listed derivatives in respect of Auckland Airport securities, including listed futures. Buying or selling one, or agreeing to do so, is a trade requiring written consent from the General Manager Corporate Affairs and is barred in blackout periods.
rules.evidence: any other listed securities of Auckland Airport or its subsidiaries, and any listed derivatives (including futures contracts listed on an authorised futures exchange) in respect of Auckland Airport securities, from time to time.

rules.detail: The Policy reaches only listed instruments. 'Trade' means buying or selling listed securities or agreeing to do so, and the definition of Restricted Securities extends to listed derivatives only. An OTC put and call written by a bank is therefore outside the definition of Restricted Securities and outside the consent and blackout regime, unless it is an associated product over unvested plan entitlements or, in substance, an agreement to sell listed shares.
rules.evidence: In this policy 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent, but it does not include subscription for, or the issue of, new securities.

rules.detail: Employees and officers who are not Restricted Persons need no consent and are not subject to blackout periods; only the insider trading prohibition, the associated products rule and the one-month short term rule apply.
rules.evidence: In addition to this Policy and Guidelines, further more specific and stringent rules also apply to trading in Auckland Airport's securities, by Directors and certain employees

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no consent or waiver route, on any associated product limiting the economic risk of an unvested entitlement under an equity based remuneration scheme. It binds every person entitled to participate in such a scheme, not just Restricted Persons, and is not limited to listed products.
rules.evidence: Where you are entitled to participate in any equity based remuneration scheme, you may not enter into any transaction for any associated product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any unvested entitlement you are eligible for under that remuneration scheme.

rules.detail: The associated products ban is drawn expressly around 'unvested entitlement', so once an entitlement has vested the ban falls away. There is no general hedging prohibition anywhere in the Policy.
rules.evidence: which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any unvested entitlement you are eligible for under that remuneration scheme

rules.section: Introduction and purpose; Trading outside black-out periods
rules.detail: A hedge executed with listed instruments is a trade in Restricted Securities, so it needs written consent, valid 10 trading days, and must be outside a blackout period.
rules.evidence: Before trading in Restricted Securities at any time outside of a blackout period, Restricted Persons must, in writing: notify Auckland Airport's General Manager Corporate Affairs of their intention to trade in securities, and seek consent to do so

rules.section: Company Policy; Transaction in associated products
rules.detail: An OTC collar over vested, unrestricted shares is neither an associated product over an unvested entitlement nor a trade in a listed security, so on the face of the Policy it is unregulated. That is a gap rather than an endorsement, and prudence points to seeking consent and disclosing the arrangement anyway, particularly given the 'If in doubt, don't' guidance and the NZ relevant-interest disclosure regime.
rules.evidence: In this policy 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent

rules.section: Company Policy; Trading outside black-out periods
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. To the extent a prepaid forward or physically settled structure is an agreement to sell listed securities, it is a trade requiring written consent and cannot be entered during a blackout period; a purely cash-settled OTC structure sits outside the definition. If it monetises an unvested scheme entitlement it is prohibited outright as an associated product.
rules.evidence: 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy and there is no speculative trading ban. A short sale of listed securities would still be a trade requiring consent for a Restricted Person, and closing it within a month would engage the short term trading rule.
Securities lending is not named and is outside the definition of 'trade', which covers only buying or selling listed securities or agreeing to do so.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Auckland Airport shares is neither a listed security nor a listed derivative, so it is outside the definition of Restricted Securities and the consent regime, though the insider trading laws and the associated products rule would still bite where relevant.
rules.evidence: any listed derivatives (including futures contracts listed on an authorised futures exchange) in respect of Auckland Airport securities

rules.detail: There is no prohibition on, or consent requirement for, margin lending. The Policy positively contemplates it: the only reference is in the exclusions, which carve a lender's enforcement disposal out of the additional restrictions on Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Restricted Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: The Policy contains no rule on granting a mortgage, charge, lien or other security over Auckland Airport securities, and creating an encumbrance is not 'buying or selling' and so not a trade requiring consent.

Secured financing over Auckland Airport shares is neither prohibited nor made subject to consent. The exclusions assume such arrangements exist and protect the executive from the consequences of a lender enforcing, which is the closest the Policy comes to addressing the topic.
rules.evidence: The additional trading restriction for Restricted Persons (as contained in this Policy) does not apply to: ... a disposal of Restricted Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Expressed as 'you should not' rather than 'must not', with a one-month window, and relief requires three sign-offs: discussion with and approval by the General Manager Corporate Affairs, plus approval by General Counsel and one of the Chief Executive or Chief Financial Officer. The one-month period is unusually short compared with the market-standard three months.
rules.evidence: You should not engage in short term trading (the buying or selling of listed securities within a one month period), unless there are exceptional circumstances discussed with and approved by Auckland Airport's General Manager Corporate Affairs and approved by General Counsel and one of the Chief Executive or the Chief Financial Officer.

clearance.approver: General Manager Corporate Affairs, on the Request for Consent to Trade in Listed Securities form (the form also carries signature blocks for the Chief Executive and Chief Financial Officer on behalf of the Company)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly following completion of any trade
clearance.section: Trading outside black-out periods; Requirements after trading
clearance.evidence: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification. A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to trading.

clearance.approver: General Manager Corporate Affairs, on a form signed by the Chair or, in the Chair's absence, the Deputy Chair; for the Chair, the form must be signed by any other Director
clearance.post_trade_to: General Manager Corporate Affairs, plus disclosure under the Securities Markets (Disclosure of Relevant Interests by Directors and Officers) Regulations and the listing rules of any relevant stock exchange
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly following completion of any trade
clearance.section: Trading outside black-out periods; Requirements after trading
clearance.evidence: In the case of proposed trading by a Director, the Request for Consent form must be signed by the Chair or, in his or her absence, the Deputy Chair and in the case of proposed trading by the Chair, the Request for Consent form must be signed by any other Director.

clearance.section: Additional Trading Restrictions for Restricted Persons
clearance.evidence: The additional trading restrictions set out below apply to: all Directors; the Chief Executive, all members of the Senior Leadership Team and their direct reports; the administrative staff of the Executive Offices; trusts and companies controlled by such persons; and anyone else notified by Auckland Airport's General Manager Corporate Affairs from time to time.

short_term.basis: the buying or selling of listed securities within a one month period
carve_outs: exceptional circumstances discussed with and approved by the General Manager Corporate Affairs and approved by General Counsel and one of the Chief Executive or the Chief Financial Officer
short_term.evidence: You should not engage in short term trading (the buying or selling of listed securities within a one month period), unless there are exceptional circumstances discussed with and approved by Auckland Airport's General Manager Corporate Affairs and approved by General Counsel and one of the Chief Executive or the Chief Financial Officer.

exceptions.evidence: This policy does not apply to: acquisitions and disposals of securities by gift or inheritance

acquisitions of securities through an issue of new listed securities, such as an issue of new debt securities or new shares on the exercise of options, under a rights issue, or a dividend reinvestment plan.

exceptions.approver: General Manager Corporate Affairs, with the circumstances deemed exceptional by the Board or its delegate
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances for these purposes include severe financial hardship, compulsion by court order or any other circumstance that is deemed exceptional by the Board.

exceptions.approver: General Manager Corporate Affairs, with the circumstances deemed exceptional by the Board or its delegate

exceptions.evidence: the following categories of passive trades: acquisition of Restricted Securities through a dividend reinvestment plan; acquisition of Restricted Securities through a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; acquisition of Restricted Securities through a rights issue
the disposal of Restricted Securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer
trading that does not result in a change to the beneficial interest in the Restricted Securities
a disposal of Restricted Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

exemption_authority: The Board may approve updates, amendments and exemptions to this Policy from time to time, implemented by written notice or posting on the intranet. Blackout waivers are sought from the General Manager Corporate Affairs and granted only where the circumstances are deemed exceptional by the Board or its delegate, or fall within severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order, and are supported by sufficient evidence that trading is the most reasonable course of action.

Insider trading laws of New Zealand and any other country where the securities may be listed, plus the listing rules of any relevant stock exchange (Auckland Airport is an ASX Foreign Exempt listing)

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Securities are Auckland Airport Ordinary Shares; debt securities issued to the public; and any other listed securities of Auckland Airport or its subsidiaries, and any listed derivatives (including futures contracts listed on an authorised futures exchange) in respect of Auckland Airport securities. 'Trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: OTC options written by a bank are neither listed securities nor listed derivatives, so the collar legs sit outside the consent and blackout machinery altogether; the constraint is the insider trading law and the unvested associated products ban, not the Policy's trading rules.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no prohibition on, or consent requirement for, margin lending, pledging or any other secured financing over Auckland Airport securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not caught by anything in the Policy, which is the single most permissive feature for a funded collar in this batch.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The additional trading restriction for Restricted Persons does not apply to ... a disposal of Restricted Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lender enforcement, including during a blackout period, is expressly outside the Restricted Person restrictions, so the bank's security can be enforced without putting the executive in breach.

bespoke_clauses.topic: associated products ban limited to unvested
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where you are entitled to participate in any equity based remuneration scheme, you may not enter into any transaction for any associated product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any unvested entitlement you are eligible for under that remuneration scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only absolute hedging ban, and it stops at vesting, so the collar must be confined to vested shares but is unconstrained once entitlements have vested.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You should not engage in short term trading (the buying or selling of listed securities within a one month period), unless there are exceptional circumstances ... approved by General Counsel and one of the Chief Executive or the Chief Financial Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A short window compared with market practice, and it is framed around buying or selling listed securities, so it constrains delivery of recently acquired shares into a settlement rather than the tenor of the OTC legs themselves.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification. A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to trading. ... where the trade is to occur during a blackout period, within [2] trading days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any listed leg or share delivery must complete within 10 trading days of consent (2 during a blackout), and the consent evaporates automatically if material information arises before execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In the case of proposed trading by a Director, the Request for Consent form must be signed by the Chair or, in his or her absence, the Deputy Chair and in the case of proposed trading by the Chair, the Request for Consent form must be signed by any other Director.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Board-level sign-off is needed for any consented trade by a Director, so the share-delivery legs of the structure require more lead time than a management approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and directors will be considered responsible for the actions of trusts and companies controlled by them. In this respect, 'control' is not to be construed in a technical way but by looking at how decisions are made in practice.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A family trust or investment company used as the collar counterparty entity is itself a Restricted Person, judged on practical rather than formal control, so it cannot be used to sidestep consent or blackout periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board may approve updates, amendments to and exemptions to this policy from time to time, which may be implemented by written notice to you and/or posting on Auckland Airport's intranet.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A general Board exemption power exists, so bespoke relief can be sought for the structure, but the same power means the permissive gaps in the Policy can be closed by notice at any time, including after the collar is in place.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The rules contained in this policy do not replace your legal obligations. ... Sometimes behaviour that you consider to be ethical actually may be insider trading. If in doubt, don't!
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy has no substance-over-form clause and no front page test, so the gaps are real, but this residual warning and the New Zealand insider trading law remain the operative constraints on entering the structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Restricted Person must comply with any disclosure obligations that person has under the Securities Markets (Disclosure of Relevant Interests by Directors and Officers) Regulations and the listing rules of any relevant stock exchange.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even though the Policy does not regulate the collar, the New Zealand relevant-interest regime is likely to require a director or officer to disclose the change in the nature of their interest arising from the security and the option legs.

summary: A funded collar is the most straightforward in this batch, because the Policy simply does not regulate the two components. There is no prohibition on, or consent requirement for, margin lending, pledging or any other secured financing over Auckland Airport securities, and the definitions of 'trade' and 'Restricted Securities' reach only listed securities and listed derivatives, so OTC put and call options written by a bank fall outside the consent regime and the blackout periods altogether. The one absolute limit is the associated products rule, which bans any product limiting the economic risk of an unvested entitlement under an equity based remuneration scheme, so the collar must cover only vested shares; and the exclusions expressly protect a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights. Practical conditions remain: no leg may be entered while holding material information, any listed leg or share delivery by a Restricted Person needs written consent from the General Manager Corporate Affairs (countersigned by the Chair for a Director) valid for 10 trading days, shares should not be bought and sold within one month, and directors and officers must still make New Zealand relevant-interest disclosure. Because the permissiveness rests on gaps rather than express permission, and the Board may amend or add exemptions by notice at any time, a bank should still obtain written confirmation from Auckland Airport before proceeding.
